The model achieves 91%, 94%, and 89% accuracy for 95% of Voc, Jsc, and FF predictions, with coefficient of determination (R2) values of 0.47, 0.77, and 0.58, respectively. By linking machine learning (ML) predictions to extracted physical parameters from the measured HOIP films optical properties, we identify key factors influencing the prediction results. We further develop separate ML-classification algorithms that identify degraded solar cells with >90% accuracies using the same optical data. This work demonstrates an efficient, nondestructive approach for HOIP solar cell assessment that can assist in accelerating the next generation of perovskite solar cell developments. We have successfully developed a solution-based interface engineering method for perovskite solar cells that yields a pristine, phase-pure n = 2 2D/3D heterostructure, eliminating excess PbI₂ and mixed 2D phases. This approach enhances energy band alignment and surface passivation, resulting in a 250% increase in surface diffusion coefficient and a 47% increase in carrier lifetime. Devices fabricated with this strategy demonstrated improved stability (80% PCE retention over 1270 hours), negligible hysteresis, and a champion power conversion efficiency of 25.3%, representing a significant advancement in scalable, high-performance perovskite photovoltaics. This advancement is detailed in: M.-C. Shih, et al., “A 2D/3D Heterostructure Perovskite Solar Cell with a Phase-Pure and Pristine 2D Layer,” Adv. Mater. 37, 2416672 (2025). 5. The two-dimensional on three-dimensional (2D/3D) perovskite bilayer heterostructure can improve the stability and performance of perovskite devices. We show that the 2D/3D perovskite stack in a device evolves dynamically during its end-of-life decomposition. Initially phase-pure 2D interlayers can evolve differently, resulting in different device stabilities. We show that a robust 2D interlayer can be formed using mixed solvents to regulate its crystallinity and phase purity. The resulting 2D/3D devices achieved 25.9% efficiency and had good durability, retaining 91% of their initial performance after 1,074 hours at 85 °C using maximum power point tracking. This advancement is detailed in: S. Tan, et al., “Spontaneous formation of robust two-dimensional perovskite phases,” Science 388, 639-645 (2025).
